goal: Establish a crash-resumable current-canvas index job lifecycle and persist AI-derived tags, relations, candidates and suppressions outside the authoritative CanvasDocument.
non_goals: Do not implement Task 16 knowledge extraction, retrieval answers or sensitive-content redaction.
Do not implement Task 17 evidence navigation, linear views or saved filters.
Do not write AI-derived tags or relations into CanvasDocument nodes or manual edges.
Do not roll back an already-saved source canvas when later extraction or overlay generation fails.
Do not add all-pairs LLM classification when the local index is unavailable.
acceptance_criteria: Canvas create/update/delete/rebuild changes enqueue revision-deduplicated index jobs transactionally with authoritative document persistence.
The local worker resets abandoned running jobs, drains ready work serially per node, applies the exact bounded retry schedule and stops cleanly.
Delete tombstones remove current anchors/embeddings; rebuild enumerates authoritative nodes and removes stale absent-node records without rewriting source content.
AI tag and approved-relation records are stored separately with finite confidence validation, exact 0.85/0.60 thresholds, stale lifecycle and semantic suppression.
Candidate recall uses the tested index interface before controlled model classification and never falls back to all-pairs model calls.
The toggleable visual overlay and feedback controls never mutate manual edges, source nodes or manual history.
Focused tests, Canvas regression, TypeScript, production build, independent review and exhaustive L2 impact pass.
notes: Use test-first implementation and keep ordinary audit reporting concise.
Retry delays are exactly 1s, 5s, 30s, 5m and then 30m capped; uniqueness is canvasId, nodeId, contentRevision and operation.
Confidence thresholds are exactly active >= 0.85, candidate >= 0.60 and < 0.85, retrieval-only < 0.60.
Task 14's canvas_ai_overlay_operations table is a transaction staging boundary; Task 15 owns durable derived overlay lifecycle tables.

L2 uses leaf data-contract entrypoints because the existing updateCanvasDocument function immediately enters unrelated global sync dynamic-dispatch boundaries; the full save/store/startup files remain required manual context and post-edit impact scope.
Use fixed UTF-8 I/O for non-ASCII reads and edits.
